deck.section_name: 13. An Introduction to AS Level Organic Chemistry
deck.title: Formulas, Functional Groups & the Naming of Organic Compounds

front_blocks.md: Define **hydrocarbon**.

back_blocks.md: A **hydrocarbon** is a compound made up of carbon and hydrogen atoms **only**.

cards.front_md: Define **hydrocarbon**.
cards.back_md: A **hydrocarbon** is a compound made up of carbon and hydrogen atoms **only**.

front_blocks.md: Why is carbon able to form such a vast number of compounds?

back_blocks.md: Carbon can form **strong covalent bonds with itself**, allowing it to form long chains, branched chains and rings — giving rise to an almost infinite variety of compounds.

cards.front_md: Why is carbon able to form such a vast number of compounds?
cards.back_md: Carbon can form **strong covalent bonds with itself**, allowing it to form long chains, branched chains and rings — giving rise to an almost infinite variety of compounds.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Ethanol is a hydrocarbon.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Ethanol contains an oxygen atom as well as carbon and hydrogen. Hydrocarbons must contain carbon and hydrogen atoms **only**.

cards.front_md:

front_blocks.md: Define **homologous series**.

back_blocks.md: A **homologous series** is a group of organic compounds that share the same functional group, with each successive member differing by CH<sub>2</sub>.

cards.front_md: Define **homologous series**.
cards.back_md: A **homologous series** is a group of organic compounds that share the same functional group, with each successive member differing by CH<sub>2</sub>.

front_blocks.md: Each successive member of a homologous series differs by **..........**. Every time a carbon is added to the chain, **..........**  hydrogen atoms are also added.

back_blocks.md: Each successive member of a homologous series differs by **CH****<sub>2</sub>**. Every time a carbon is added to the chain, **two** hydrogen atoms are also added.

cards.front_md: Each successive member of a homologous series differs by **..........**. Every time a carbon is added to the chain, **..........**  hydrogen atoms are also added.
cards.back_md: Each successive member of a homologous series differs by **CH****<sub>2</sub>**. Every time a carbon is added to the chain, **two** hydrogen atoms are also added.

front_blocks.md: Define **alkane**.

back_blocks.md: **Alkanes** are the simplest hydrocarbons, containing only carbon and hydrogen atoms joined by **single covalent bonds** with no functional group.

cards.front_md: Define **alkane**.
cards.back_md: **Alkanes** are the simplest hydrocarbons, containing only carbon and hydrogen atoms joined by **single covalent bonds** with no functional group.

front_blocks.md: What is the general formula of the alkane homologous series?

back_blocks.md: The general formula is **C**<sub>**n**</sub>**H**<sub>**2n+2**</sub>, where n is the number of carbon atoms.

cards.front_md: What is the general formula of the alkane homologous series?
cards.back_md: The general formula is **C**<sub>**n**</sub>**H**<sub>**2n+2**</sub>, where n is the number of carbon atoms.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Alkanes can be linear, branched or cyclic in structure.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Alkanes can exist as **linear**, **branched** or **cyclic** structures, all containing only C–C and C–H single bonds.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Alkanes can be linear, branched or cyclic in structure.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

Alkanes can exist as **linear**, **branched** or **cyclic** structures, all containing only C–C and C–H single bonds.

front_blocks.md: Methane has **..........**  carbon atom(s) and the formula **..........**, while pentane has **..........**  carbon atoms and is a liquid at room temperature.

back_blocks.md: Methane has **one** carbon atom and the formula **CH****<sub>4</sub>**, while pentane has **five** carbon atoms and is a liquid at room temperature.

cards.front_md: Methane has **..........**  carbon atom(s) and the formula **..........**, while pentane has **..........**  carbon atoms and is a liquid at room temperature.
cards.back_md: Methane has **one** carbon atom and the formula **CH****<sub>4</sub>**, while pentane has **five** carbon atoms and is a liquid at room temperature.

front_blocks.md: Define **functional group**.

back_blocks.md: A **functional group** is a specific atom or group of atoms in an organic molecule that determines its physical and chemical properties.

cards.front_md: Define **functional group**.
cards.back_md: A **functional group** is a specific atom or group of atoms in an organic molecule that determines its physical and chemical properties.

front_blocks.md: What does the letter R represent in organic structural formulae?

back_blocks.md: **R** represents any other atom or group of atoms in the molecule, **except hydrogen**.

cards.front_md: What does the letter R represent in organic structural formulae?
cards.back_md: **R** represents any other atom or group of atoms in the molecule, **except hydrogen**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
All members of a homologous series share the same functional group and general formula.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
A **homologous series** is a group of organic compounds sharing the same **functional group**, the same **general formula** and the same chemical properties.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

All members of a homologous series share the same functional group and general formula.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

A **homologous series** is a group of organic compounds sharing the same **functional group**, the same **general formula** and the same chemical properties.

front_blocks.md: Define **general formula**.

back_blocks.md: A **general formula** is an algebraic formula using letters and numbers that represents an entire **homologous series** of compounds.

cards.front_md: Define **general formula**.
cards.back_md: A **general formula** is an algebraic formula using letters and numbers that represents an entire **homologous series** of compounds.

front_blocks.md: The **..........**  formula shows how atoms are bonded to each carbon atom, while the **..........**  formula is a 2D representation showing all atoms and all bonds.

back_blocks.md: The **structural** formula shows how atoms are bonded to each carbon atom, while the **displayed** formula is a 2D representation showing all atoms and all bonds.

cards.front_md: The **..........**  formula shows how atoms are bonded to each carbon atom, while the **..........**  formula is a 2D representation showing all atoms and all bonds.
cards.back_md: The **structural** formula shows how atoms are bonded to each carbon atom, while the **displayed** formula is a 2D representation showing all atoms and all bonds.

front_blocks.md: What is the skeletal formula and how does it differ from the displayed formula?

back_blocks.md: The **skeletal formula** is a simplified displayed formula in which all C–H bonds and carbon symbols are removed, leaving only the carbon skeleton and functional groups.

cards.front_md: What is the skeletal formula and how does it differ from the displayed formula?
cards.back_md: The **skeletal formula** is a simplified displayed formula in which all C–H bonds and carbon symbols are removed, leaving only the carbon skeleton and functional groups.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The displayed formula of a molecule shows only the carbon skeleton with functional groups highlighted.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The **displayed formula** shows **all** atoms by their symbols and **all** bonds. It is the **skeletal** formula that removes C–H bonds and carbon symbols.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

The displayed formula of a molecule shows only the carbon skeleton with functional groups highlighted.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

The **displayed formula** shows **all** atoms by their symbols and **all** bonds. It is the **skeletal** formula that removes C–H bonds and carbon symbols.

front_blocks.md: Organic molecules are classified by their dominant **..........**. Compounds with the same functional group but differing by **..........**  per member form a **..........** series.

back_blocks.md: Organic molecules are classified by their dominant **functional group**. Compounds with the same functional group but differing by **CH****<sub>2</sub>** per member form a **homologous** series.

cards.front_md: Organic molecules are classified by their dominant **..........**. Compounds with the same functional group but differing by **..........**  per member form a **..........** series.

front_blocks.md: Give the general formula for alkanes and explain what n represents.

back_blocks.md: The general formula of alkanes is **C**<sub>**n**</sub>**H**<sub>**2n+2**</sub>, where **n** is the number of carbon atoms in the molecule.

cards.front_md: Give the general formula for alkanes and explain what n represents.
cards.back_md: The general formula of alkanes is **C**<sub>**n**</sub>**H**<sub>**2n+2**</sub>, where **n** is the number of carbon atoms in the molecule.

front_blocks.md: Define **stem (organic nomenclature)**.

back_blocks.md: A **stem** is the part of an organic compound's name that indicates the number of carbon atoms in the **longest chain** of the molecule (e.g. meth- = 1, eth- = 2, prop- = 3).

cards.front_md: Define **stem (organic nomenclature)**.
cards.back_md: A **stem** is the part of an organic compound's name that indicates the number of carbon atoms in the **longest chain** of the molecule (e.g. meth- = 1, eth- = 2, prop- = 3).

front_blocks.md: When numbering the carbon chain to name an organic compound, which end do you start from?

back_blocks.md: Number from the end that gives the **lowest possible locant numbers** to the substituents or functional groups.

cards.front_md: When numbering the carbon chain to name an organic compound, which end do you start from?
cards.back_md: Number from the end that gives the **lowest possible locant numbers** to the substituents or functional groups.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Side chains are named by changing the -ane ending of the parent alkane to -yl.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
For example, a methane-derived side chain becomes a **methyl** group and an ethane-derived side chain becomes an **ethyl** group.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Side chains are named by changing the -ane ending of the parent alkane to -yl.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

For example, a methane-derived side chain becomes a **methyl** group and an ethane-derived side chain becomes an **ethyl** group.

front_blocks.md: When two identical side chains are present, the prefix **..........**  is used. When three identical side chains are present, the prefix **..........**  is used.

back_blocks.md: When two identical side chains are present, the prefix **di-** is used. When three identical side chains are present, the prefix **tri-** is used.

cards.front_md: When two identical side chains are present, the prefix **..........**  is used. When three identical side chains are present, the prefix **..........**  is used.
cards.back_md: When two identical side chains are present, the prefix **di-** is used. When three identical side chains are present, the prefix **tri-** is used.

front_blocks.md: What IUPAC suffix is used for ketones, and what suffix is used for carboxylic acids?

back_blocks.md: Ketones take the suffix **-one** (e.g. propanone) and carboxylic acids take the suffix **-oic acid** (e.g. ethanoic acid).

cards.front_md: What IUPAC suffix is used for ketones, and what suffix is used for carboxylic acids?
cards.back_md: Ketones take the suffix **-one** (e.g. propanone) and carboxylic acids take the suffix **-oic acid** (e.g. ethanoic acid).

front_blocks.md: Define **aliphatic compound**.

back_blocks.md: An **aliphatic compound** is an organic compound with a straight or branched carbon chain, including cyclic compounds that do **not** contain a benzene ring.

cards.front_md: Define **aliphatic compound**.
cards.back_md: An **aliphatic compound** is an organic compound with a straight or branched carbon chain, including cyclic compounds that do **not** contain a benzene ring.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
When naming a compound with two different alkyl side chains, the side chains are listed in order of increasing chain length.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
When different alkyl side chains are present, they are listed in **alphabetical order**, not by chain length.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

When naming a compound with two different alkyl side chains, the side chains are listed in order of increasing chain length.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

When different alkyl side chains are present, they are listed in **alphabetical order**, not by chain length.

front_blocks.md: In systematic nomenclature, numbers are separated from words by a **..........**  and adjacent numbers are separated from each other by a **..........** .

back_blocks.md: In systematic nomenclature, numbers are separated from words by a **hyphen** and adjacent numbers are separated from each other by a **comma**.

cards.front_md: In systematic nomenclature, numbers are separated from words by a **..........**  and adjacent numbers are separated from each other by a **..........** .
cards.back_md: In systematic nomenclature, numbers are separated from words by a **hyphen** and adjacent numbers are separated from each other by a **comma**.

front_blocks.md: What are the IUPAC prefixes used for fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine substituents in halogenoalkanes?

back_blocks.md: The prefixes are **fluoro-**, **chloro-**, **bromo-** and **iodo-** respectively, placed before the parent chain name with the locant number.

cards.front_md: What are the IUPAC prefixes used for fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine substituents in halogenoalkanes?
cards.back_md: The prefixes are **fluoro-**, **chloro-**, **bromo-** and **iodo-** respectively, placed before the parent chain name with the locant number.

front_blocks.md: Define **molecular formula**.

back_blocks.md: A **molecular formula** shows the actual number and type of each atom present in one molecule of a compound.

cards.front_md: Define **molecular formula**.
cards.back_md: A **molecular formula** shows the actual number and type of each atom present in one molecule of a compound.

front_blocks.md: Define **empirical formula**.

back_blocks.md: An **empirical formula** shows the simplest whole number ratio of the elements present in one molecule of a compound.

cards.front_md: Define **empirical formula**.
cards.back_md: An **empirical formula** shows the simplest whole number ratio of the elements present in one molecule of a compound.

front_blocks.md: What is the molecular formula of ethanoic acid and what does it tell you?

back_blocks.md: The molecular formula of ethanoic acid is **C**<sub>**2**</sub>**H**<sub>**4**</sub>**O**<sub>**2**</sub>, showing that one molecule contains **2 carbon**, **4 hydrogen** and **2 oxygen** atoms.

cards.front_md: What is the molecular formula of ethanoic acid and what does it tell you?
cards.back_md: The molecular formula of ethanoic acid is **C**<sub>**2**</sub>**H**<sub>**4**</sub>**O**<sub>**2**</sub>, showing that one molecule contains **2 carbon**, **4 hydrogen** and **2 oxygen** atoms.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The empirical formula and molecular formula of a compound are always the same.

back_blocks.md: **False.**

The empirical formula gives the simplest ratio of atoms, while the molecular formula gives the actual number. For example, ethanoic acid has molecular formula C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>O<sub>2</sub> but empirical formula **CH**<sub>**2**</sub>**O**.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

The empirical formula and molecular formula of a compound are always the same.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

The empirical formula gives the simplest ratio of atoms, while the molecular formula gives the actual number. For example, ethanoic acid has molecular formula C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>O<sub>2</sub> but empirical formula **CH**<sub>**2**</sub>**O**.

front_blocks.md: The **..........**  formula shows the actual number of atoms in a molecule, while the **..........**  formula shows the simplest whole number ratio of those atoms.

back_blocks.md: The **molecular** formula shows the actual number of atoms in a molecule, while the **empirical** formula shows the simplest whole number ratio of those atoms.

cards.front_md: The **..........**  formula shows the actual number of atoms in a molecule, while the **..........**  formula shows the simplest whole number ratio of those atoms.
cards.back_md: The **molecular** formula shows the actual number of atoms in a molecule, while the **empirical** formula shows the simplest whole number ratio of those atoms.

front_blocks.md: How do you convert a molecular formula into an empirical formula?

back_blocks.md: Divide the number of each type of atom by their **highest common factor** to give the simplest whole number ratio.

cards.front_md: How do you convert a molecular formula into an empirical formula?
cards.back_md: Divide the number of each type of atom by their **highest common factor** to give the simplest whole number ratio.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Ethanol (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O) and ethanoic acid (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>O<sub>2</sub>) have the same empirical formula.

back_blocks.md: **False.**

Ethanol (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O) has empirical formula **CH**<sub>**3**</sub>**O**, while ethanoic acid (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>O<sub>2</sub>) has empirical formula **CH**<sub>**2**</sub>**O**. They are different.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Ethanol (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O) and ethanoic acid (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>O<sub>2</sub>) have the same empirical formula.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Ethanol (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O) has empirical formula **CH**<sub>**3**</sub>**O**, while ethanoic acid (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>O<sub>2</sub>) has empirical formula **CH**<sub>**2**</sub>**O**. They are different.

front_blocks.md: To find the empirical formula from percentage composition, first convert the percentages to **..........**  of atoms by dividing by the **..........**  of each element.

back_blocks.md: To find the empirical formula from percentage composition, first convert the percentages to **moles** of atoms by dividing by the **relative atomic mass** of each element.

cards.front_md: To find the empirical formula from percentage composition, first convert the percentages to **..........**  of atoms by dividing by the **..........**  of each element.
cards.back_md: To find the empirical formula from percentage composition, first convert the percentages to **moles** of atoms by dividing by the **relative atomic mass** of each element.

front_blocks.md: Glucose has the molecular formula C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>. What is its empirical formula?

back_blocks.md: The empirical formula of glucose is **CH**<sub>**2**</sub>**O**, obtained by dividing all subscripts by the highest common factor of 6.
